findings.highlight: It made me wonder if always doing the right thing is actually a twisted way to live.
findings.evidenceJa: 正義の味方として、ひどく歪なのではないかと。
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether he is deeply distorted as a would-be hero, in light of the suggestion that this war fulfills his desire.
findings.explanation: Shirou's doubt about his own motives as a hero becomes doubt about the value of always doing right.

findings.highlight: Shirou Emiya always does the right thing.
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮士郎は正義の味方に。
findings.governingReading: The fragment reasserts the vow: Shirou Emiya will become a champion of justice, for the sake of people unjustly killed.
findings.explanation: A future identity as a champion of justice becomes habitual correct behavior.

findings.highlight: Apparently, Servants can turn into invisible ghosts, but alas, I never learned how do to that trick.
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントは霊体になれるらしいが、生憎俺にはそんな芸当はさせられない。
findings.governingReading: He understands that Servants can become spirit bodies, but unfortunately he cannot make or allow Saber to perform that feat.
findings.explanation: Shirou's inability to make Saber dematerialize becomes his failure to learn to become a ghost.

findings.highlight: Saber gives a straightforward response as she scrutinizes me.
findings.evidenceJa: まっすぐにこっちを見ながら、淡々とセイバーは言う。
findings.governingReading: She speaks matter-of-factly while looking straight at him.
findings.explanation: Saber looking directly at Shirou becomes scrutinizing him.

findings.highlight: With Saber in that outfit, I can't help but actually think she's real now.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの服装はあまりにも現実感がありすぎて、否応なしに異性を意識してしまうのだ。
findings.governingReading: The everyday reality of Saber's clothes makes Shirou involuntarily conscious of her as a woman.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes a sense of Saber's reality for explicit awareness of her as a woman. The surrounding attraction remains, and this belongs in a dossier about Shirou's perception.

findings.highlight: "Wh-what the hell! If I hadn't intervened, you'd have been cut in half!"
findings.evidenceJa: 「な、なんだよそれ！　あの時はああでもしなけりゃおまえが斬られてたじゃないか！」
findings.governingReading: Shirou protests that Saber would have been cut if he had not intervened.
findings.explanation: Being cut becomes being cut in half.

findings.highlight: If it's true, I'll need to respect Saber's needs and actions as best I can.
findings.evidenceJa: なら俺は、自分に出来る範囲でセイバーに応えるしかない。
findings.governingReading: Because she cannot choose her Master, Shirou concludes he must answer or live up to Saber as far as he is able.
findings.explanation: Responding to Saber within Shirou's abilities becomes respecting her needs and actions.

findings.highlight: They have their own reasons for serving Masters.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らにも目的があるから、交換条件としてマスターに仕えている。
findings.governingReading: Shirou understands that Heroic Spirits have their own objective and serve Masters as the other side of a bargain.
findings.explanation: Serving under an exchange condition becomes serving for unspecified reasons.

findings.highlight: You said any means possible, right? Does that mean you..."
findings.evidenceJa: 可能である全ての手段っと言ったな。それは勝つ為には手段を選ばないって事か。たとえば—」
findings.governingReading: He asks whether using every possible means means choosing no limits to win, then begins an example.
findings.explanation: Shirou's question about refusing no means is left unfinished in English.

findings.highlight: He said that people who have nothing to do with Masters would be drawn into the conflict, and the tragedy of ten years ago would be repeated...
findings.evidenceJa: マスターでもない無関係の人間を巻き込んで、十年前のあの日のような惨状を起こすような—
findings.governingReading: Recalling the priest's explanation, Shirou imagines involving uninvolved non-Masters and causing a disaster as examples of the means he fears Saber might use.
findings.explanation: Shirou's imagined example of an unacceptable tactic becomes a prediction reported from Kotomine. Saber's reply still rejects the tactic, making the English transition less direct.

findings.highlight: I can only do things I allow myself to. It is impossible for me to betray my own beliefs. Harming unarmed innocents goes against a knight's oath."
findings.evidenceJa: 私は私が許す行為しか出来ない。自分を裏切る事は、私には不可能です。剣を持たぬ人間に傷を負わせる事など、騎士の誓いに反します」
findings.governingReading: Saber says harming humans who bear no weapon violates a knight's oath.

findings.highlight: Each of us made a name for ourselves in our respective time periods; we accomplished some great deed beyond human capabilities.
findings.evidenceJa: それぞれが“自分の生きた時代”で名を馳せたか、或いは人の身に余る偉業を成し遂げた者たち。
findings.governingReading: Servants either won fame in their own era or achieved a deed beyond what a human body can accomplish.
findings.explanation: Alternative routes to Heroic Spirit status become universal combined requirements.

findings.highlight: Whatever the means, we are beings who have sublimated to deity-esque status."
findings.evidenceJa: どのような手段であれ、一個人の力だけで神域まで上り詰めた存在です」
findings.governingReading: Whatever the means, each rose as far as the divine realm solely by one person's power.
findings.explanation: Reaching the divine domain by an individual's power alone loses the individual-power condition.

findings.highlight: Heroic Spirits had supernatural abilities while they were alive, were celebrated after their deaths, and promoted to a higher spiritual rank than a ghost or such.
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊とは、生前に卓越した能力を持った英雄が死後に祭り上げられ、幽霊ではなく精霊の域に昇格したモノを言う。
findings.governingReading: A hero possessed outstanding abilities while alive, was exalted after death, and rose from ghost to spirit.
findings.explanation: Exceptional living ability becomes supernatural ability.

findings.highlight: "Correct. There may be some Heroic Spirits who possess multiple attributes, but I would say in all humility that there are none better than I with the sword."
findings.evidenceJa: 「はい。属性を複数持つ英霊もいますが、こと剣に関しては私の右に出る者はいない、と自負しています」
findings.governingReading: She openly prides herself that, regarding swordsmanship, no one surpasses her.
findings.explanation: Saber's proud self-assessment is presented as humility.

findings.highlight: If you can't beat your opponent with a sword, you just have to come up with another way.
findings.evidenceJa: 剣で敵わない相手なら、剣以外で敵の息の根を断つだけの話じゃないか。
findings.governingReading: If a foe cannot be beaten with a sword, Shirou realizes one can cut off that foe's life by something other than a sword.
findings.explanation: Killing by another means becomes merely finding another way.

findings.highlight: "Ah, so you can't reveal your name, huh? Yeah, you're right. Like hypnosis or being hit with a Whisper-type spell, or... Well, I doubt it, but if other Masters have Mystic Eyes, then I might start babbling about it.
findings.evidenceJa: 「ああ、名前は明かせないって事か。……そうだな、たしかにその通りだ。催眠とか暗示とか、いないとは思うけど他のマスターに魔眼持ちがいたらベラベラ秘密を喋りかねないし。
findings.governingReading: Shirou lists hypnosis, suggestion and the possibility of another Master's Mystic Eyes as ways his thoughts could be compromised.
findings.explanation: Generic suggestion becomes an invented Whisper-type spell.

findings.highlight: "Ah... Are you certain you should make such a rash decision?"
findings.evidenceJa: 「ぁ—その、本当に、そんなにあっさりと？」
findings.governingReading: Saber asks whether he truly agrees so readily or simply.
findings.explanation: An unexpectedly ready agreement becomes a rash decision.

findings.highlight: "I do not know how you saw it. Your standards are what sets how you measure a Servant's ability. There are some Masters who distinguish simply through colors, and there are other Masters who understand by comparing them to beasts."
findings.evidenceJa: 「どのようなカタチで把握したのかは知りません。サーヴァントの能力を測るのは、あくまでシロウが見る基準です。単純に色で識別するマスターもいれば、獣に喩えて見分けるマスターもいます」
findings.governingReading: How a Master represents a Servant's ability depends on that Master's own perceptual standard.
findings.explanation: The explanation of personal measurement standards is grammatically malformed.
